comments.note: The hostname format check (line 238, config.ts) tests the raw `host` value before trimming. This is intentional and correct — any whitespace in the host field (even leading/trailing) is rejected outright. The subsequent `host.trim()` for length checks and final storage is consistent with this intent.

The regex /[/\\\0\s]/ correctly catches tab and newline characters via \s, not just space. This was confirmed via manual validation. No additional test cases are strictly required, but adding tab/newline test variants would strengthen documentation.

Port-suffixed hostnames (e.g., 'github.com:8080') and IP addresses ('192.168.1.1') pass the hostname validation regex — this is correct behavior since colons, digits, and dots are all valid. No concern here.

summary: Reviewed 3 modified files (src/server/routes/config.ts, src/server/__tests__/routes/config.test.ts, docs/agents/project-manifest/constraints.md). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium findings. 2 Low / Info observations recorded. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01 — Broken Access Control: No access-control layer exists on any /api/config/* endpoint (no authentication middleware, no session checks). This is a pre-existing architectural characteristic of the tool — it appears to be a local developer tool, not a multi-tenant server. The WP-004 change does not introduce or worsen this posture. No new IDOR or privilege-escalation vectors are introduced by the hostname validation guard. Info only; no action required for this WP.

A02 — Cryptographic Failures: Plaintext PATs are stored in config.json. This is a known, documented design decision (see constraints.md and config/README.md). Mitigation already in place: saveConfigField() applies chmod 600 on POSIX after every write (src/config/config.ts line 316-318), and all API responses pass tokens through buildMaskedCredentials() (showing only last 4 chars). The WP-004 change does not alter token storage or transmission. Info only.

A03 — Injection: The hostname validation guard (config.ts line 238) uses /[/\\\0\s]/.test(host) to reject forward slash, backslash, null bytes, and whitespace before the value is persisted. This directly prevents path-traversal injection via the host field. No SQL, template, or OS-command injection vectors are present in the credential routes — values are persisted as JSON and never interpolated into shell commands at this layer. All four forbidden-character cases are tested (forward slash, backslash, null byte, whitespace). PASS.

A04 — Insecure Design: The hostname format validation (reject /, \, \0, \s) is applied to the raw host value before trim(), which is correct security posture — any whitespace anywhere in the field, including leading/trailing, causes an immediate 400 rejection. The subsequent host.trim() used for length checking and persistence is consistent with this intent. No logic flaws identified in the validation flow.

A05 — Security Misconfiguration: Error messages in the credential routes use static, field-name-based messages (e.g., 'Invalid field "host": must not contain...'). No stack traces, internal file paths, or sensitive runtime state are leaked in error responses. sendError() wraps the message in { error: string } with no additional metadata. PASS.

A07 — Identification & Authentication Failures / A09 — Security Logging: Credential mutation operations (create, update, delete) are audit-logged via errorLogManager?.append() with Severity: 'warning', Source: 'credential-audit'. The audit entries include id, label, host but deliberately never include the token value — this is explicit in the code comments (lines 310, 355). The hostname validation guard does not bypass this audit path. PASS.
